segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so for the 42 users you have today plus the 12 warehouse leads, the pricing sheet puts you at 54 seats. That keeps you in the same tier, $38 per user per month, annual term.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. We were assuming 55 because one of the quality managers may need access too. Is there any issue if we start with 54 and add one in November?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No issue. The extra seat would just prorate from the day you add it through the May 31 term end. For one seat, you're talking roughly $266 if it starts November 1.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That's fine. On billing, we need the invoice dated after July 1. Our new fiscal year starts then, and payables will kick it back if it's in June.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, we can set the invoice date as July 2. The order form can be signed this week, but billing won't run until then.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. And the go-live date is still August 19, right? We have the plant shutdown the week before, so we don't want training during that window.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, August 19 for go-live. Training would be August 6 and 7, two ninety-minute sessions, recorded, with your supervisors invited.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Contract term is one year, no auto-renewal, same data processing terms as the master agreement from last year?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That's right. One-year term, July 2 through July 1 next year, no auto-renewal, and the existing master terms carry over. The order form will just reference them.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, send that over at 54 seats with the July invoice date. If it matches what we discussed, I can get it signed by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send the order form this afternoon: 54 seats, $24,624 annual subscription, July 2 invoice date, August 19 go-live, and the two training sessions listed.
